plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium bid in a first-price auction is (n-1)/n × value = 2/3 × value. My value is $46, so optimal bid ≈ $30.7. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitively bidding given my high value.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, i.e., 2/3 * value. This balances the trade-off between winning probability and profit margin. My value is $17, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 * 17 ≈ $11.30 to maximize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $28, so I should bid approximately 28 * (2/3) ≈ $18.7 to balance the probability of winning against overpaying. This maximizes expected profit given the symmetric equilibrium strategy for uniform value auctions with 3 bidders.
